advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconsider the AST token-presence pin in `test_the_committed_tree_assertions_consult_marker_admission`; it couples to sibling-test structure and breaks on behavior-preserving refactors (helper extraction / rename of `markers_for`).
evidence: `if isinstance(node, ast.Constant): return isinstance(node.value, str) and "admitted" in node.value`
Rule-4 litmus: extracting the assertion into a helper or renaming `markers_for` preserves behavior yet fails this pin, so it would break on a behavior-preserving refactor.
The commit message itself concedes 'This is a SOURCE-level pin on purpose' and that the behavioral alternative was rejected.
advisory.finding: The new test `test_the_committed_tree_assertions_consult_marker_admission` is a change-detector: it walks the AST of two other test functions and asserts they contain the string constant 'admitted' or a reference/attribute named `markers_for`, coupling to the internal token structure of sibling tests rather than to any observable behavior. A behavior-preserving refactor (e.g. extracting an `_assert_admitted(out)` helper that checks 'admitted' internally, or renaming `markers_for`) would break it while the contract still holds.
scenarios: A future refactor factors the 'admitted' check into a shared helper `_assert_admitted(out)` used by both committed-tree tests — the AST pin no longer sees a literal 'admitted' constant in the function body and fails despite the contract still being enforced.
`markers_for` is renamed (e.g. to `admitted_markers`) with call sites updated — the pin fails without any behavior change.

Docstring claim `# Read the AST, not the text: a comment mentioning admission must not satisfy this pin` is only true for comments; string literals (docstrings/messages) ARE in the AST and DO satisfy branch (a).
The pin's own litmus fails: it cannot distinguish 'the widened assertion is present' from 'a string literal happens to contain admitted'.
dropped.finding: The AST pin's _consults treats any ast.Constant string containing the substring 'admitted' as proof the assertion consults marker admission, but docstrings and assert-message string literals are also ast.Constant nodes. For test_check_passes_on_the_committed_tree this means a future revert to the defective `assert "new=0" in out` form still passes the pin so long as any string literal in the function mentions 'admitted' — the fail-open the change exists to close.
scenarios: A later contributor reverts line 96 back to `assert "new=0" in out and "increased=0" in out` but the function docstring or an assert message still contains the word 'admitted' — the pin stays green while the assertion is once again blind to markers.
dropped.suggested_fix: Walk only the assertion test expressions (collect ast.Assert nodes and inspect node.test) instead of the whole function tree, or require both a 'markers_for' reference AND the widened disjunct rather than accepting a bare substring in any Constant.
